subject: general
question: Which of the following began with a revolt of the military soldiers at Meerut, soon became widespread and posed a grave challenge to the British rule?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Indian Mutiny (1857)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Mutiny of 1857 began with a revolt of the military soldiers at **Meerut**.
 
• The mutiny quickly spread to other parts of India, including Delhi, Kanpur, and Lucknow, posing a grave challenge to British rule.
 
• The rebellion was characterized by widespread civilian participation, making it one of the first major movements against British colonial rule.
 
• The revolt had various causes, including political, economic, social, and military grievances against the British East India Company.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Battle of Panipat (1761)**

 
 
• The Battle of Panipat was fought between the Maratha Empire and the Durrani Empire led by Ahmad Shah Abdali.
 
• It was one of the largest and bloodiest fought battles in the 18th century.
 
• This battle marked the end of the Maratha Empire's expansion.
 
• The loss weakened the Maratha Empire considerably and paved the way for British dominance in India.
 
 
 
• **Quit India Movement (1942)**
 
 
• The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on August 8, 1942, during World War II.
 
• The movement aimed at demanding an end to British rule in India.
 
• It was marked by mass protests, strikes, and acts of civil disobedience.
 
• Despite being suppressed by the British, the movement played a crucial role in India's struggle for independence.
 
 
 
• **Battle of Plassey (1757)**
 
 
• The Battle of Plassey was fought between the British East India Company and the Nawab of Bengal, Siraj-ud-Daulah.
 
• It took place on June 23, 1757, and ended in a decisive victory for the British East India Company.
 
• This battle marked the beginning of British colonial rule in India.
 
• The victory was aided by the betrayal of Siraj-ud-Daulah's commander, Mir Jafar.
